notes:
VERIFIED 2026-11-11 (storecheck.py): Nova3D sells through Shopify at store.nova3dp.com, not www.nova3dp.com (the corporate site, which links its 'Store' to store.nova3dp.com). The Awin deep-link host needs checking. Whale4 Ultra 16K variants: US $399.99 (list $899.99) NOT available; EU $399.99 not available; JP $699 available; CN $699 available; AU $421.13 available. Product text: 10-inch 16K, 15120 x 6230, 14 x 19 µm, 211.68 x 118.37 x 220 mm, resin heating plus air purifier, one-step leveling. The maker spec page says ball screw, 100 mm/h, 24 kg. A storecheck search the same day (product level, no variant split) listed: GEM3 Max Jewelry $1,599 (list $1,899), GEM3 Max Dental $1,599, Master $1,599, Tough Washable resin $30.99, Ultra-Clear resin $36.99, and a 3DMakerpro Seal ($649) and Seal Lite ($359) resold there. US-variant availability for these is UNVERIFIED: every variant lookup returned HTTP 429, including the final delayed retry of the GEM3 Max Dental. Snippets mark the GEM3 Max Jewelry, the GEM3 Dental, and GEM3 Max LCD/film spares 'Sold out' on the US storefront. Shipping policy: free express from an unnamed 'oversea warehouse'; China-warehouse orders pay their own shipping and customs. The refund-policy page is warranty-repair text only and gives no warranty length or return window. Trustpilot: 3.2 from 2 reviews; the newest (Dec 2024, 2 stars) says Nova3D gave no reply and no order update after payment.

PAGE PLAN FOR A RE-RUN (only if the Whale4 US variant is back in stock): query 'best 16k resin 3d printer'. Today's results are mostly affiliate listicles on unrelated domains, so the slot is thin. Shopper segments and honest winners:
(1) Most proven all-rounder: Elegoo Saturn 4 Ultra 16K. Same 14 x 19 µm panel and same build volume, plus tilt release, auto-leveling, a 1080p AI camera and a heated vat. 3DWithUs scored it 4.6/5 and saw no failures at -3 to 4 °C room temperature. It has no air filter. Elegoo store $649.99 (2026-11-11), or $538 bundled with the Mercury Plus V2.0 wash station. Not an approved program: name it without a link.
(2) Lowest price for a 10-inch 16K with heater and filter: Nova3D Whale4 Ultra at $399.99, if the US variant is buyable. 3DWithUs scored it 4.5/5, with a 30 °C heater, a carbon filter, gravity auto-fill and factory pre-leveling. Cons: plastic vat, no mid-print setting changes, 54 lb.
(3) Rival on price: Anycubic Photon Mono M7 Pro (14K, 10.1-inch, heated vat) at $489 on the Anycubic store, 2026-11-11.
(4) Bigger plate: Phrozen Sonic Mighty Revo 16K MAX, 14-inch 16K, $1,600 at us.phrozen3d.com (Phrozen is approved as awin:phrozen); or Uniformation GK3 Ultra, 13.5-inch, 20 x 26 µm, about $1,310-1,400 (from snippets, unverified).

Pain points, counted loosely from about 12 sources: failed prints in cold rooms (5: Creative Bloq, Loot Studios, 3DWithUs x2, printer-hub), fumes and smell (4: Lemmy x2, Hackaday, Loot Studios), and whether 16K is visibly better than 9K/12K (4: Fauxhammer, OpenELAB, Elevated Systems via recap, guide snippets). Most say pixel size and reliability matter more than the K number. Saturn 4 Ultra 16K complaints (printer-hub, Elevated Systems recap; not independently checked): false foreign-matter alerts, heater errors, adhesion and a warped plate.

JEWELRY ANGLE REJECTED: I found no independent evidence that the GEM3 or GEM3 Max wins any segment. The only test is from BlueCast, a resin seller (under 1% part variance across the plate). The GEM3 Max uses the same 14 x 19 µm 16K panel as $400-650 printers and costs $1,599. The GEM3 has square 17 x 17 µm pixels and a 154 x 87 x 120 mm build (reseller page), around $1,299 per a snippet (unverified). For hobby jewelers, Phrozen's own guide and others point to the Sonic Mini 8K/8K S (22 µm, about $350 per Tom's Hardware); pros point to Formlabs or Asiga.
